hook: SCP-184 is a palm-sized metal dodecahedron that makes the inside of any enclosed space keep growing while the outside stays the same. Picture your house quietly getting bigger every night and you have the appeal. The file is short, so read the addenda closely for where the object has been.
whyItMatters: It packs the bigger-on-the-inside idea into a single small object with a clear, escalating rule. One addendum suggests that it, or something with the same effect, could be the source of other anomalous locations in the setting, which turns a trinket into a possible origin for a whole family of places. Tying its recovery to a real city known in the text for explosive growth gives the fiction a grounded anchor.
thingsToNotice:
The description moves from orderly expansion to breakdown: glass books, a wooden microwave, doors that open onto blank walls, corridors that shrink or loop into mazes. That decay is more unsettling than the growth, because it suggests the object copies without understanding what it copies.

The recovery note reveals that the object was found in the Kowloon Walled City, held by someone whose identity is expunged, and that papers point to it being rented out to households at fifty pounds per half hour. Residents meet investigators with a wall of silence, and police destroyed affected blocks before anyone could study them, so the city's true fate stays unknown. The containment, a magnet disguised as a statue in a fake park, is a practical answer to an object that can never be kept inside any structure.
